# Root list test vectors

Fixtures for the [signed root list and the CA bundle](../../docs/reference/root-list.md): root lists that a host must accept or refuse, given the list it already holds, and CA bundles with their trust sequence, with the expected outcome and reason code of each in `v1/manifest.json`.

The roots are the test roots of the [hand-off vectors](../hand-off/README.md): A and B are active, C is a root that some lists add, Z is on no list. `pki/` holds copies of their certificates and OpenPGP primaries, `removals/` the removal authorisation of A, B and C as the holder would store them, and the list `seq7-a` is the root list of the trust sequence the hand-off answers carry (7). Everything under `v1/` is public material made with throw-away software keys by `../hand-off/generate.py`, in the same run as the hand-off set; no private key is kept. The record digests in the lists are made up. A change to a vector that flips its outcome is a new format version (a new directory).

`just check-vectors` checks that the manifest names every tracked file, that the pins match the root files, that every list carries the signatures of its `signers` and that they verify except in the tampered one, that every removal authorisation is valid except the one a case refuses, and that each bundle holds the roots it names under its trust sequence.

## What the cases add

- **The same list again** ([record 0006](../../docs/decisions/0006-bundle-history-and-trust-files.md), rule 50; [the root list page](../../docs/reference/root-list.md#how-a-host-reads-it)). After a root left, a list that is byte for byte the held one passes: `same-list-again-after-a-revoke` (`seq8-b-without-a`, which carries a removal) and `same-list-again-after-a-retire` (`seq8-ab-without-a`, which the retired root signed). Checks 8 to 10 do not run for it; the clock check does. `same-list-again-with-an-unknown-signer-beside-a-trusted-one` is accepted: the held list again, with a second signature by Z, a root key on no list (the bytes of `root-list.json` are those of `seq7-a`); `same-list-again-after-its-expiry` is refused with `expired` (the host also warns `held-expired`).
- **The dates of a list** ([record 0006](../../docs/decisions/0006-bundle-history-and-trust-files.md), rule 49; [the root list page](../../docs/reference/root-list.md#how-a-host-reads-it)). In every list of this set, and of the SSH CA key list set, `expires_at` is exactly 13 calendar months after `signed_at` (the same day and time, or the last day of the month), and no case has a candidate that is signed after its clock, except the one that says so with its own `flaw` (`way-back-signed-after-the-clock`, below); no list had to be corrected. Three lists break one rule each, and the manifest names the break in their `flaw`: `seq7-a-expires-13m1s` and `seq7-a-expires-12m` (`expires_at-not-13-months`) and `seq7-a-signed-in-the-future`, signed one second after the clock of its case (`signed_at-after-clock`). Each is refused with `malformed`, in the cases `expires-13-months-and-a-second-after-signing`, `expires-12-months-after-signing` and `signed-after-the-clock`, which give their clock. `update` is the case at the boundary: `seq7-a` is signed at the clock. The end of a month: lists signed on 2026-01-31, 2027-01-30 and 2028-02-29 expire on 2027-02-28, 2028-02-29 and 2029-03-29 and are accepted (`signed-on-the-31st-of-january`, `signed-on-the-30th-of-january-before-a-leap-year`, `signed-on-a-leap-day`, each at its own signing time); the lists with the expiry that a plain month addition gives (2027-03-03 and 2028-03-01) are refused with `malformed` (`expires-by-plain-month-addition-from-the-31st`, `expires-by-plain-month-addition-from-the-30th`).
- **CA bundles** ([record 0006](../../docs/decisions/0006-bundle-history-and-trust-files.md), rule 52; [the root list page](../../docs/reference/root-list.md#how-a-host-reads-it)). A case with `bundle` also checks that CA bundle against the candidate list (`--ca-bundle`): `ca-bundle-of-the-list` and `ca-bundle-after-a-revoke` are accepted. A bundle whose certificate holds the key of root A but does not verify with its own key (signed by the key of Z) is `ca-bundle-7-signed-by-another-key`, and one that verifies with its key and says it is not a CA certificate is `ca-bundle-7-not-a-ca`; the manifest names the break in their `flaw` (`not-signed-by-its-own-key`, `not-a-ca`), and the cases `ca-bundle-certificate-signed-by-another-key` and `ca-bundle-certificate-not-a-ca` refuse them with `ca-bundle-mismatch`. Each differs from `ca-bundle-7` in the certificate of A only. Three bundles differ from it in the certificates, and one in the first line: `ca-bundle-7-extra-certificate` (A, B and C), `ca-bundle-7-missing-certificate` (A only), `ca-bundle-7-wrong-order` (B, then A) and `ca-bundle-8-of-list-7` (the certificates of `seq7-a` under the first line `# trust-sequence: 8`); the cases `ca-bundle-with-a-certificate-too-many`, `ca-bundle-with-a-certificate-missing`, `ca-bundle-in-the-wrong-order` and `ca-bundle-with-the-wrong-first-line` refuse them with `ca-bundle-mismatch`, and the manifest names their flaw (`extra-certificate`, `missing-certificate`, `wrong-order`, `wrong-sequence`). `ca-bundle-7-issuer-is-another-name` has the key of A, is signed by it and is a CA certificate, and names another issuer than its subject (the flaw `issuer-not-subject`); `ca-bundle-certificate-names-another-issuer` refuses it with `ca-bundle-mismatch`: a root certificate names itself as its issuer.
- **The lowest sequence for initial pins** ([record 0006](../../docs/decisions/0006-bundle-history-and-trust-files.md), rule 51; [the root list page](../../docs/reference/root-list.md#how-a-host-reads-it)). A case with `min_sequence` is a host that holds only its initial pins and was given a lowest sequence to accept (`--min-sequence N`); it has no held list. `initial-pins-lowest-sequence-above` (8, for a list of sequence 7) is refused with `rollback`; `initial-pins-lowest-sequence-equal` (7) is accepted.
- **What check 5 also refuses** ([record 0006](../../docs/decisions/0006-bundle-history-and-trust-files.md), rule 49; [the root list page](../../docs/reference/root-list.md#how-a-host-reads-it)). Each list differs from `seq7-a` (or `seq8-b-without-a`) in one thing, is signed validly, and is refused with `malformed` against a held list; the manifest names the fault in its `flaw`: `label-twice` (`seq7-a-label-twice`, the label A twice), `pin-twice` (`seq7-a-pin-twice`), `fingerprint-wrong-form` (an upper-case OpenPGP fingerprint), `last-record-digest-wrong-form` (a digest of 63 digits), `sequence-0` (`seq0-a`, against initial pins: check 5 comes before the sequence), `pin-twice-in-removals` (`seq8-b-without-a-removal-twice`) and `empty-authorisation` (`seq8-b-without-a-empty-authorisation`). The cases carry the names of the faults.
- **The way back** ([record 0006](../../docs/decisions/0006-bundle-history-and-trust-files.md), rule 53; [the root list page](../../docs/reference/root-list.md#how-a-host-reads-it)). After check 5 a host takes a list without checks 6 and 7 when the list removes at least one root key of the held list and has an entry in `removals` for every root key it removes. A host that holds only pins never does. A case gives `wayback`, true, only when the list was accepted although check 6 or check 7 would have refused it: its sequence is lower than the held list's, or equal to it with other content. A list that names a removed key and has a higher sequence has no `wayback`. A key is removed when its pin is on the held list and not on the new one, and an entry is for a key by its pin; labels and fingerprints are not compared. The checks other than 6 and 7 run as before, so the first one that fails gives the code. Thirty-one lists and thirty-five cases hold it. Every new list is signed on 2026-11-15 at 12:00:00Z and expires 13 calendar months later. The clock of a case is 2026-12-01T12:00:00Z (the signing time of `seq8-b-without-a`) unless the case gives another.
  - *Held lists.* A name starts with the sequence of the list; `max` is 9007199254740991, the highest sequence a list may carry. `seqmax-ab-by-a` and `seqmax-abc-by-a` are what a thief makes with one stolen root key A: the same root keys as before, one signature, the highest sequence. `seq8-ab-by-a` is the same at sequence 8. The lists `seq5-ab`, `seq5-ac`, `h3-bc`, `h4-bcz` and `seq1-b-without-c` stand for histories: `h2-abc`, `h3-bc` and `h4-bcz` are three in a row (A leaves after the first, Z is added in the third, B and C stay), and `seq5-ac` has A again beside C.
  - *Accepted, with `wayback`.* A list without A that B signs and that names A: `way-back-from-the-highest-sequence` (held at the highest sequence) and `way-back-at-the-sequence-of-the-thief` (held at the same sequence with other content). A list that revokes A and is signed by A and B, with A named: `revoke-signed-by-the-key-with-its-entry`. A list that retires B and names it: `retire-with-the-authorisation`. Two keys removed and both named: `two-removed-both-named`. A list that removes one key and adds another: `way-back-that-also-adds-a-key`. An entry for the removed key with another label, a kept key with another label and a kept key with another `openpgp_fingerprint`: `way-back-entry-with-another-label`, `way-back-with-a-new-label` and `way-back-with-a-new-fingerprint`. A held list that has expired, with the clock after its `expires_at` and before the candidate's: `way-back-over-an-expired-held-list`.
  - *Accepted by design.* These show what the rule lets through, and they are no flaw of the vectors: `one-key-and-one-authorisation-by-design` (one stolen key, A, and the stored authorisation of B replace the set at a low sequence; `the-same-takeover-at-the-next-sequence` shows that the same list at the next sequence is accepted without `wayback`, as before the rule) and `way-back-removing-every-held-key` (the same takeover, with every held key removed and a removed key signing; record 0006, rules 53 and 10); `way-back-chain-lowers-the-sequence-step-1` and `way-back-chain-lowers-the-sequence-step-2` (a way back that lowers the sequence, then an older public list that passes the ordinary checks; the thief already holds a current root key and a stored authorisation; record 0006, rule 19); `old-revoke-list-after-its-key-came-back` (it looks like a replay, and the host cannot see that A was added again; record 0006, rule 54 is what closes it, in the writer).
  - *Refused with `rollback`.* The list is not a way back, so check 6 refuses it: a lower sequence that removes nothing (`lower-sequence-removes-nothing`, and `lower-sequence-with-a-new-label-removes-nothing`, where only a label changes); a retire with no entry (`no-entry-is-not-the-way-back`, also the revoke that the removed key signs and that has no entry); a list that removes two keys and names one (`two-removed-one-named`); old lists that were published (`old-list-as-published`), with the signature of a key that came later (`old-list-with-the-signature-of-a-later-key`), and that removes a later key (`old-list-that-removes-a-later-key`); and a host with only pins and a lowest sequence, also for a list that names the key it removes (`pins-keep-their-lowest-sequence`, `pins-keep-their-lowest-sequence-for-a-named-removal`).
  - *Refused by a check that still runs.* `way-back-with-a-signature-missing` and `way-back-with-a-new-label-the-kept-key-not-signing` (`insufficient-signers`, check 10); `way-back-with-another-keys-authorisation`, `extra-entry-for-a-key-not-held` and `entry-for-a-key-that-stays` (`removal-invalid`, check 9: naming decides, check 9 judges, so a bad entry is not `rollback`); `removal-list-signed-only-by-a-new-key` (`unknown-signer`, check 2) and `way-back-with-a-second-signer-on-no-list` (`unknown-signer`, check 8); `way-back-list-changed-after-signing` (`signature-invalid`, check 3); `way-back-after-its-expiry` (`expired`, check 11, clock 2028-01-02T12:00:00Z); `way-back-signed-after-the-clock` (`malformed`, check 5, clock 2026-11-30T12:00:00Z, before the `signed_at` of `seq8-b-without-a`; the case has the `flaw` `signed_at-after-clock`, because other cases use the list at a later clock).
  - *What `just check-vectors` adds for it.* A case has `wayback` exactly when it accepts a list with a lower sequence than the held list's, or the same sequence and other bytes; such a list removes a root key of the held list and has an entry in `removals` for every root key it removes. A case refused with `removal-invalid` holds an authorisation that is not valid by itself, or an entry for a root key that the held list does not have or that the list keeps.
- **The warning of an expired held list** is `held-expired` in the case `held-list-expired`, and in the like cases of the SSH CA key list set (`held-list-expired`) and the CRL set (`held-crl-expired`), as the pages name it. It was `expired` before.

`just check-vectors` also checks the dates of every list against its `flaw`, that each CA bundle certificate verifies with its own key and is a CA certificate unless its bundle has a `flaw`, and that the members `bundle` and `min_sequence` of a case agree with the list and the bundle it names.

The expected result of each case of this set was checked against the command `ritueel verify root-list` of the Go code on 2026-11-14 (run again on the built command, with the CA bundle check) (the lists, the CA bundles and the lowest sequence; the clock of each case). The cases of the way back are not in that sentence: they follow record 0006, rule 53 and the order of the checks of the page, and the test of `internal/rootlist` runs them.

**Rules that have no vector yet**, and why:

- A signature file or a CA bundle of more than 256 KiB (and the read limit of 8 MiB), and a `root-list.json` of more than 256 KiB: a file that large does not belong in the tree.
- A signature by a key that is not P-384 (`signature-invalid`): a root key on a list is P-384 by the root profile, and the pin of a key that is not P-384 would have to be on the list the host holds; the generator makes only P-384 root keys.
- What the host does not enforce (the canonical form, `last_record_sha256` above sequence 1, the order of `roots` and `removals`, a removal entry's label, an empty `removals`) and an entry with no `openpgp_fingerprint`: these are accepted today and no case states them.
- The exit codes of the command for a file that is missing, a link, a FIFO or a folder, and which check a file over 256 KiB reaches: the manifest gives the outcome and the code of a check, not a failure of the command.

**Planned, not files yet.** These vectors are for the writer (`apply`, `revoke` and `check history`, [record 0006](../../docs/decisions/0006-bundle-history-and-trust-files.md), rules 53 and 54, and [record 0007](../../docs/decisions/0007-changing-and-losing-a-root.md), rule 12). They need a bundle and a plan, not a list and a held list, so each is a test of the writer that builds its own bundle; the setup and the answer are below, and no file of this set holds them. The root keys are A and B. A row that is tested is a test of the builder in `internal/trustset`: where it says that `apply` or `revoke` refuses, the builder refuses with the same code and writes nothing, and the command that uses it comes later. The two rows that need the engine to read a bundle stay planned.

| Name | Setup | Expected | State |
|---|---|---|---|
| `root-returns-after-a-revoke` | trust sets `{A,B}`, then `{B}` (A revoked); a plan adds A's pin | `apply` refuses with `root-returns` and writes nothing | tested in `internal/trustset`: `TestRootReturns/root-returns-after-a-revoke` |
| `root-returns-after-a-retire` | trust sets `{A,B}`, then `{B}` (A retired); a plan adds A's pin | `apply` refuses with `root-returns` | tested in `internal/trustset`: `TestRootReturns/root-returns-after-a-retire` |
| `root-returns-under-a-new-label` | as `root-returns-after-a-revoke`, with A's pin under the label C | `apply` refuses with `root-returns` | tested in `internal/trustset`: `TestRootReturns/root-returns-under-a-new-label` |
| `root-returns-after-several-lists` | A was revoked three lists earlier | `apply` refuses with `root-returns` | tested in `internal/trustset`: `TestRootReturns/root-returns-after-several-lists` |
| `root-returns-after-an-emergency-revoke` | the trust set without A was written by `revoke`, so no ceremony record lists it; a plan adds A | `apply` refuses with `root-returns` and writes nothing, because record 0006, rule 54 reads every trust set | tested in `internal/trustset`: `TestRootReturns/root-returns-after-an-emergency-revoke` |
| `root-returns-with-the-old-fingerprint-under-a-new-pin` | trust sets `{A,B}`, then `{B}` (A revoked); a plan adds a new key whose entry has A's `openpgp_fingerprint` | `apply` refuses with `root-returns` and writes nothing | tested in `internal/trustset`: `TestRootReturns/root-returns-with-the-old-fingerprint-under-a-new-pin` |
| `check-history-finds-a-key-that-came-back` | a bundle whose newest root list holds a pin that an earlier list held and the list before it did not | the finding `root-returns`, exit code 3 | planned |
| `check-history-reads-a-trust-set-no-record-lists` | the set written by `revoke` (no ceremony record) drops A; a later set adds A | the finding `root-returns` | planned |
| `revoke-carries-the-authorisation-when-the-key-signs` | a revoke of a key that can sign, whose stored authorisation is there | the list has the entry for the key, and the `.jws` has no signature of the revoked key | tested in `internal/trustset`: `TestEveryKind/revoke-carries-the-authorisation-when-the-key-signs` |
| `retire-carries-no-authorisation` | a retire | the list has no `removals` | tested in `internal/trustset`: `TestEveryKind/retire-carries-no-authorisation` |
| `revoke-without-the-authorisation-when-the-key-signs` | the stored authorisation of A is missing and A can sign | `revoke` goes on, A signs the list, the list has no `removals`, and `revoke` warns that the list names no key | tested in `internal/trustset`: `TestEveryKind/revoke-without-the-authorisation-when-the-key-signs` |
| `revoke-of-two-keys-one-has-neither` | two keys: one has its stored authorisation, the other has none and cannot sign | `revoke` refuses and writes nothing | tested in `internal/trustset`: `TestSignersAreCheckedBeforeAnyKey/revoke-of-two-keys-one-has-neither` |
